October 4–12, 2025 · Motorcycle tour

Seven Days Through Northern California & Oregon

A ~1,100-mile loop from the Golden Gate up the redwood coast, across southern Oregon, down past Mount Shasta and Lassen, and home through Napa and Sonoma wine country.

  • ~1,100miles
  • 7riding days
  • 2states
  • 2rounds of golf
1San Francisco → Ukiah, CA2Ukiah → Crescent City, CA3Crescent City → Klamath Falls, OR4Klamath Falls → Red Bluff, CA5Red Bluff → Sonoma, CA6Sonoma → Napa7Napa → San Francisco
Day1

Sat, Oct 4

San Francisco → Ukiah, CA

~150 mi · 4 hrs

Scenic ride via US-101 and CA-1 N, mixing coastal beauty, redwoods, and small towns.

  1. Golden Gate Bridge — North Vista Point photos
  2. Marin Headlands — bridge and coast views; winding roads
  3. Stinson Beach — beach and lagoon stop
  4. Point Reyes National Seashore — cliffs and waves; optional lighthouse detour (~20 mi)
  5. Tomales Bay — bay views and oyster farms
  6. Bodega Bay — harbor, seafood, “The Birds” film site; exhilarating CA-1 curves
  7. Bodega Dunes — windswept trails
  8. Sebastopol — orchards and farm stands via CA-12 E
  9. Santa Rosa Historic District — tree-lined streets
  10. Kendall-Jackson Wine Estate & Gardens — tasting and gardens (~7 mi from Santa Rosa)
  11. US-101 N through Mendocino vineyards
  12. Hendy Woods State Park — redwood detour on CA-128
  13. Ukiah Valley — Mayacamas Mountains at sunset

Riding tips

Early morning / late afternoon for golden light and less fog. CA-1 is tight and thrilling but watch for fog and wind; US-101 is faster and straighter. Plan 1–2 stops (Stinson Beach, Bodega Bay, Kendall-Jackson) for the ~3 hr 53 min ride. Fuel at Bodega — stations are sparse on CA-1.

Weather outlook

Coast (SF, Stinson, Bodega) 60–70°F (15–21°C), warming to 70–80°F (21–27°C) inland. Partly cloudy with morning coastal fog (visibility under 100 ft possible) clearing by afternoon; 10–20% chance of light showers. Winds 5–15 mph, stronger on the coast. Nights 45–55°F (7–13°C). Start after 9 AM to avoid fog.

Potential dangers & how to avoid them 5
  • Coastal fog on CA-1. Dense morning fog near Stinson Beach / Point Reyes reduces visibility; use low beams/fog lights and slow down. Avoid a pre-9 AM start if foggy (check Caltrans QuickMap).
  • Tight curves / wet pavement. CA-1’s sharp turns (e.g., near Bodega) get slick from fog and drizzle; stay focused and avoid gravel shoulders. US-101 is straighter but watch vineyard winds.
  • Construction. Northbound US-101 reduced to 1 lane ~2–3 mi north of SR-271 (Mendocino Co.) 24/7 — expect delays. One-way traffic control near Arnold possible 7 AM–5 PM.
  • Wildlife. Deer active in Marin/Sonoma at dawn and dusk (e.g., Hendy Woods); slow down in forested areas.
  • Fuel / other. Sparse stations on CA-1; fill in SF or Sausalito. No landslides forecast, but watch for fall debris.
Day2

Sun, Oct 5

Ukiah → Crescent City, CA

~240 mi · 4.5 hrs

The Redwood Highway (US-101 N) through forests, coast, and towns.

  1. Ukiah wine country — vineyards and oaks
  2. Willits — “Gateway to the Redwoods”
  3. Laytonville — redwood canopy
  4. Avenue of the Giants — 31 mi through Humboldt Redwoods SP; Founder’s Grove, Rockefeller Loop
  5. Garberville / Scotia — Eel River views
  6. Eureka — Victorian town; Old Town marina detour
  7. Arcata Bay / Humboldt Lagoons — wetlands, ocean vistas; elk at Elk Prairie
  8. Prairie Creek Redwoods State Park — meadows and redwoods
  9. Del Norte Coast Redwoods State Park — ocean pullouts
  10. Trees of Mystery, Klamath — Paul Bunyan statue and gondola
  11. Battery Point Lighthouse — sunset tides

Riding tips

4–5 hours without stops; plan 6–8 with sights. Tight curves in the redwoods and along the coast; fog and wet roads are common in the morning. Fuel in Ukiah, Willits, or Eureka (scarce in the redwoods). Watch for elk and deer.

Potential dangers & how to avoid them 2
  • Fog / rain in redwoods and coast. Morning fog and drizzle on US-101 near Eureka / Del Norte; use fog lights and consider delaying the start to 10 AM. Fallen leaves and needles make curves slick.
  • Fuel. Limited between Garberville and Eureka — fill early. No major closures, but check for debris in the redwoods.
Day3

Mon, Oct 6

Crescent City → Klamath Falls, OR

~200 mi · 4 hrs

US-199 (Redwood Highway) to Grants Pass, OR-238 through the Applegate Valley to Medford, then OR-140 to Klamath Falls.

  1. Jedediah Smith Redwoods SP — Stout Grove detour on Howland Hill Rd
  2. Smith River — turquoise water and cliffs; Patrick Creek Overlook
  3. Collier Tunnel — winding and narrow
  4. Applegate Valley — vineyards, orchards; Applegate Lake stop
  5. Optional: Oregon Caves National Monument — OR-46 detour (~20 mi) to marble caves
  6. Fish Lake / Lake of the Woods — mountain lakes on OR-140
  7. Optional: Crater Lake National Park — ~70 mi round trip; Rim Drive vistas

Riding tips

3.5–4 hours base; 5–7 with detours. Curvy and twisty on US-199 and OR-46; low traffic on OR-238. Fuel in Grants Pass or Medford. Bring layers for coastal chill and inland warmth.

Potential dangers & how to avoid them 2
  • Fog / wet roads. Morning fog on US-199 (Jedediah Smith); be careful on curves and in the tunnel. OR-46 (Caves detour) is narrow and slick when wet — skip it if raining.
  • Twisty sections / wildlife. Tight turns on US-199 / OR-46 — watch for gravel and debris. Deer and elk in Applegate / Lake of the Woods at dawn and dusk. OR-140 width-restricted to 14 ft (6 AM–7 PM Mon–Fri) near Klamath Falls for construction, ending Oct 15.
Day4

Tue, Oct 7

Klamath Falls → Red Bluff, CA

~250 mi · 4.5 hrs

US-97 S to Mount Shasta, CA-89 S / CA-44 through Lassen Volcanic National Park to Redding, then I-5 S to Red Bluff.

  1. Upper Klamath Lake — wetlands and pelicans
  2. Klamath Basin Grasslands — open vistas
  3. Mount Shasta — vista point near Weed; optional CA-89 detour via McCloud for river and falls
  4. Burney Falls — 129-ft cascade in the state park
  5. Hat Creek Valley — lava fields and Lassen Peak views
  6. Lassen Volcanic NP — Manzanita Lake, Sulphur Works, Bumpass Hell, Kings Creek / Summit Lake
  7. Shingletown — oak woodlands
  8. Redding — Sacramento River and Sundial Bridge
  9. Red Bluff — Victorian charm on the river

Riding tips

6–8 hours with stops. Thrilling CA-89 switchbacks; bring layers for the elevation swings. Fuel in Klamath Falls, Weed, Burney, or Redding.

Weather outlook

Klamath Falls / Mount Shasta 65–80°F (18–27°C), partly cloudy, 5–10% rain; morning fog near the lake clears. Lassen highs 60–75°F (15–24°C), 10–15% chance of showers at elevation. Red Bluff 70–85°F (21–29°C), sunny. Winds 5–15 mph. Lows 40–60°F (4–15°C). Dry overall, but watch Lassen for flurries.

Potential dangers & how to avoid them 3
  • Elevation weather. Sudden changes in Lassen (CA-89); light rain or snow possible at the peaks — check NPS road status (usually open in October, but early snow can close it). Be careful on wet switchbacks.
  • Wildlife / curves. Deer and bears in Lassen and Burney; slow down in forests. CA-89 / CA-44 descents are tight. Watch gravel shoulders and wildlife at dawn and dusk.
  • Heat. 85°F+ in Red Bluff — hydrate. I-5 is straightforward but crosswinds are possible.
Day5

Wed, Oct 8

Red Bluff → Sonoma, CA

~180 mi · 3.5 hrs

I-5 S to Williams, CA-20 W to Clearlake, CA-53 S / CA-29 S to Calistoga, then CA-12 W to Sonoma.

  1. Sacramento Valley farms — almond and rice fields, Sierra views
  2. CA-20 rolling hills and oaks to Clear Lake — Mount Konocti volcano
  3. CA-53 — lake views and Lower Lake towns
  4. Napa Valley on CA-29 — vineyards, Mayacamas Mountains, balloons, Calistoga springs
  5. CA-12 oak hills and horse ranches to Sonoma Plaza

Riding tips

Balances straight I-5 cruising with CA-20 / CA-12 curves. Go early for fewer tourists. Watch for winery traffic and cyclists on CA-29 / CA-12.

Golf

Eagle Vines Golf Club

3:00 PM tee time · 707-257-4470

3 rental club sets secured

Weather outlook

Red Bluff / Williams 70–85°F (21–29°C), sunny. Clearlake / Sonoma 65–80°F (18–27°C), partly cloudy with 5–10% showers; morning fog near Calistoga clears. Winds 5–15 mph (crosswinds on I-5). Lows 45–60°F (7–15°C). Perfect wine-country weather.

Potential dangers & how to avoid them 3
  • Crosswinds / traffic. Open I-5 stretches are gusty (15–20 mph) — lean in. Heavy tourist traffic on CA-29 / CA-12 (winery pullouts, cyclists), especially afternoons.
  • Curves / roadwork. Moderate twists on CA-20 / CA-12 near Clear Lake and Sonoma; gravel possible if damp. Utility work on CA-20 at Clearlake Oaks (one-way 8 AM–4 PM, ~5-min delays) and nighttime paving on CA-29 west of Lower Lake.
  • Wildlife. Deer on CA-20 / CA-12 at dawn and dusk. No major I-5 issues.
